## Codex Review (GPT-5.4)

This remains a `new-component` PR with secondary tags `public-api`, `docs`, `tests`, and `a11y`. I re-reviewed the full branch against a freshly fetched `upstream/master` and reran `pnpm test:jsdom OTPField --no-watch`, `pnpm test:chromium OTPField --no-watch`, `pnpm typescript`, and `pnpm eslint` on the current head.

### 1. Remaining Bugs / Issues (None)

I do not currently see any remaining actionable correctness or API issues on the branch head.

### 2. Public API & Composition Assessment

The public shape is now much cleaner than the original branch state. Making `OTPField.Root` the grouping element, keeping `length` as the single source of truth, exposing a single-string value, and leaving forwarded `aria-*` on the root gives the component a more coherent long-term contract than the earlier `Root` + `Group` split.

### 3. Accessibility and Interaction Assessment

The interaction model looks solid at this point: canceled changes no longer move focus, forward delete reselects the shifted value, invalid rejected input preserves selection, readonly slots still participate in focus tracking and keyboard navigation, and the root/label wiring is internally consistent. For a preview component, the keyboard and focus behavior now looks well covered.

### 4. Previous Review Issues Status

| Prior review item | Status | Notes |
|---|:---:|---|
| Canceled changes still moved focus | Resolved | Focus/completion side effects now flush only against committed values |
| Custom validation needed better flexibility | Resolved | `inputMode` and `onValueInvalid` are both present and documented |
| `Group` made the public structure heavier than necessary | Resolved | `Root` now owns the group semantics and the docs/tests match that model |
| Generated OTP reference JSON was unnecessary noise | Resolved | The OTP docs now rely on `types.md` only |
| Readonly slots lost Arrow/Home/End navigation | Resolved | Navigation keys now still work while readonly editing remains blocked |

### Merge Confidence Score

Overall merge confidence is 5/5. I do not see remaining blockers, and the branch now has strong coverage for the keyboard, focus, validation, docs, and form-integration paths that carry most of the risk for this component.

> I'm not quite sure I follow the logic that decides when the text is selected or not

It should always be selected if you navigate via keyboard or click into an already-filled input. I actually can't get into the state you got in in the recording when pressing <kbd>Backspace</kbd> - it's always selected in that case 🤔

> In the video above, there's a moment when I press numbers inside an input but nothing happens. Does it happen because the text inside the input is not selected? It felt surprising.

I can't get into the state where this happens, do you have the exact steps/keys?

> What's the use case for OTPField.Group? Is there a scenario where several of them would be used? If that's the case, a demo would be nice.

It's mainly to match `NumberField` which has `Root` and `Group` parts. It's possibly not as necessary as NumberField since there's no `ScrubArea` part, so the Root itself could be `role="group"`. This would likely be less confusing regarding how ARIA roles get forwarded as well.

> It should always be selected if you navigate via keyboard or click into an already-filled input.

So is it expected that the last input gets selected when filling it?

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/65d25096-ff75-4f54-9866-39d63f772f88

> I actually can't get into the state you got in in the recording when pressing Backspace - it's always selected in that case
> I can't get into the state where this happens, do you have the exact steps/keys?

You can see the exact keys being pressed in the video, but I can reproduce it consistently with this sequence:

1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, ⬅️, Del: at this point the selection is lost and pressing any number doesn't have an effect.

> It's mainly to match NumberField which has Root and Group parts. It's possibly not as necessary as NumberField since there's no ScrubArea part, so the Root itself could be role="group". This would likely be less confusing regarding how ARIA roles get forwarded as well.

Sounds like it's worth considering removing it.

> So is it expected that the last input gets selected when filling it?

I would say it's ambiguous for this particular case because there's no new input to move to and so it selects because it's filled and focused. It probably looks better without it though, so I'll try to stop it in this case.

> 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, ⬅️, Del: at this point the selection is lost and pressing any number doesn't have an effect.

On macOS, is <kbd>Backspace</kbd> the same as  <kbd>Del</kbd> or is it different?  It's likely `'Delete'` vs. `'Backspace'` path, will look into it. As it doesn't happen here:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1f0a252e-b052-4a74-88cc-b58860f95854

> On macOS, is Backspace the same as Del or is it different? It's likely 'Delete' vs. 'Backspace' path, will look into it. As it doesn't happen here:

On macOS, <kbd>Backspace</kbd> (backward delete ⌫)  and <kbd>Delete</kbd> (forward delete ⌦) are different, yes.

> On macOS, Backspace (backward delete ⌫) and Delete (forward delete ⌦) are different, yes.

I don't think I've ever used forward delete on macOS 🙈 fixed it though, <kbd>fn + delete</kbd> is the command on a MBP keyboard

I was curious to see if https://github.com/guilhermerodz/input-otp/issues/92 would be an issue here. It behaves like this with Bitwarden:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9f7f9eda-24ba-4e89-9d3e-67a6e3551b11

Even though Shadcn UI uses https://github.com/guilhermerodz/input-otp, the experience is a bit better:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f6cd660d-99d2-4f03-ba02-ae6ddfdb816e

It's the last input that is focused at the end. So overall it's OK, it works (and in the future, we have room to push it one step further).

## Critical Issues (1 found)

  - [error-handling] User-supplied sanitizeValue callback can throw, crashing the component tree. It's called unguarded from 6 locations including during render (otp.ts:58-59). If it throws, the entire tree
  unmounts with no indication the callback is the culprit.

## Important Issues (5 found)

  - [error-handling] clipboardData.getData('text/plain') called without null guard (OTPFieldInput.tsx:250). In edge cases clipboardData can be null, causing a TypeError.
  - [types/validation] length prop typed as number with no dev-mode validation for positive integers. Values like 0, -1, 3.7, NaN, Infinity produce silent degradation. This is the most important invariant of the
  component — everything depends on it. Add a dev warning similar to the existing inputCount !== length warning.
  - [types/DX] sanitizeValue is silently ignored when validationType is not 'none' (otp.ts:56-60). No runtime warning for this misconfiguration — developers will be confused.
  - [tests] No unit tests for otp.ts utility functions (normalizeOTPValue, replaceOTPValue, removeOTPCharacter, stripOTPWhitespace). These are pure foundational functions that are cheap to test and critical to
  correctness. Edge cases like Unicode/emoji, negative length, out-of-bounds index are untested.
  - [tests] onValueInvalid and onValueComplete not tested for paste interactions. The paste codepath has distinct logic and fires different reason values (input-paste) that are part of the public API contract.

## Suggestions (8 found)

  - [tests] No test for data-complete attribute presence/absence on root and inputs (7/10 criticality)
  - [tests] Paste into a middle slot is untested — exercises the splice logic in replaceOTPValue (6/10)
  - [tests] Delete/Backspace not verified as blocked in readOnly mode (6/10)
  - [tests] No negative test for orphaned <OTPField.Input> context error (5/10)
  - [comments] data-focused on Input means "any input in the group is focused", not "this specific input" — description should clarify (OTPFieldInputDataAttributes.ts:9)
  - [comments] onValueInvalid JSDoc says "clamped" which could mislead — truncation to length does not trigger this callback (OTPFieldRoot.tsx:618)
  - [comments] id prop JSDoc should mention derived IDs for subsequent inputs ({id}-2, {id}-3)
  - [docs] types.md auto-generated onValueChange description has list items concatenated into unreadable text (generation tooling issue)

## Strengths

  - Project guideline compliance is excellent. useStableCallback, useIsoLayoutEffect, useTimeout, shadow DOM utilities, ownerDocument — all used correctly. No violations found.
  - Discriminated event detail types are well-crafted. The .spec.tsx files prove narrowing works via @ts-expect-error annotations.
  - Controlled/async pattern is solid. The pendingFocusRef/pendingCompleteValueRef pattern correctly handles race conditions where external state updates arrive asynchronously.
  - Context design is clean — no mutable refs exposed (unlike NumberFieldRootContext), and getOTPFieldInputState is a nice helper for deriving child state.
  - Error message in OTPFieldRootContext.ts follows the required "Base UI:" format perfectly and is registered in error-codes.json.
  - Comprehensive test coverage of value handling, keyboard nav, form integration, accessibility, SSR, disabled/readOnly states, and cancel/veto patterns.

@flaviendelangle a few good points there, but a bunch are not relevant. For the "critical error", we shouldn't swallow the sanitize error as users should handle it themselves.

Updated the branch

Codex:
```
A lot of this is stale or over-rotated against the current branch.

What I’d treat as real:
- `#2` `onValueInvalid` wording: fair. “sanitized” is a bit broader than what actually triggers it.
- `#10` readonly paste test: fair small gap if it’s still not covered.
- `#11` complete-to-complete transition test: fair regression test to add.
- `#12` `OTPFieldInputState` using `Omit<...>`: reasonable type-clarity cleanup, but not urgent.
- `#4` `clipboardData.getData()` try/catch: optional hardening, not critical.

What I would not take:
- `#1` catch `sanitizeValue` throws: no. User callback exceptions crashing normally through React is standard; swallowing them would hide the real bug.
- `#5` warn when `autoSubmit` can’t find a form: maybe, but low-value and noisy.
- `#6` warn when `focusInput` target ref is null: no, too noisy/internal.
- `#7` throw for invalid `length`: no. Dev warning is enough.
- `#8` `onValueChange` throwing: not a component bug.
- `#13` document internal `setValue` return semantics: internal context, not worth it.

What looks outdated / incorrect now:
- `#3` broken `types.md` formatting for `onValueChange`: this was already improved.
- `#9` no Separator tests: `Separator` is just a re-export; I wouldn’t add OTP-specific conformance for that.
- `#22` docs should mention first input `aria-label` is stripped: not true anymore on the current branch, since we changed to warn rather than silently strip.
- `#24` demo should use `useTimeout`: stale; we intentionally did not go that route.
- `#25` sanitizeValue in memo deps: not really actionable.
```

### 1. Silent clipboard paste failure — bare catch block

  [silent-failure-hunter] HIGH — OTPFieldInput.tsx:277-281

  The `onPaste` handler calls `preventDefault()` (killing native paste), then wraps `clipboardData.getData()` in a bare catch that silently returns. If clipboard access is denied (e.g., SecurityError on mobile browsers), the user presses Ctrl+V and nothing happens — no feedback, no console message.

```
  event.preventDefault();  // native paste already killed
  try {
    rawValue = event.clipboardData?.getData('text/plain') ?? '';
  } catch {       // bare catch, no logging
    return;       // silent return
  }
```

  Recommendation: At minimum, log the error in development so developers can diagnose clipboard permission issues.

### 2. autoSubmit silently does nothing when no form is found

  [silent-failure-hunter] MEDIUM — OTPFieldRoot.tsx:179-192

  When `autoSubmit={true}` and the OTP completes, `requestSubmit()` silently no-ops if the field isn't inside a `<form>` and no form prop is provided. A dev-mode warning (matching the existing pattern for length mismatch) would save debugging time.


## Test Coverage Gaps

  - onValueComplete via keyboard reason (criticality 8/10) — The REASONS.keyboard complete path is untested. A Backspace + retype sequence that refills the OTP should verify onValueComplete fires with the correct
  reason.
  - Hidden input onValueInvalid (8/10) — The hidden input's onChange independently calls onValueInvalid during autofill, but this path is untested. The "password manager autofill" test only checks
  onValueChange/onValueComplete.
  - Paste completing from a middle slot (7/10) — Existing paste-to-complete test only pastes from slot 0. Pasting from a non-zero index exercises a different branch in replaceOTPValue.
  - data-disabled / data-readonly state attributes (5/10) — Tests verify the native disabled/readonly attributes but not the data-* state attributes used for CSS styling.
  - useOTPFieldRootContext error when used outside Root (5/10) — The descriptive error thrown by the context is untested.

## Comment Improvements

  - OTPFieldInput.tsx:107 — `maxLength: index === 0 ? length : 1` — Add a comment explaining the first input accepts the full length for browser autofill support.
  - otp.ts:66 — `Array.from(sanitizedValue).slice(...)` — Add a comment noting this handles multi-byte/surrogate-pair characters correctly (vs. `String.slice` which counts UTF-16 code units).

> 1. Silent clipboard paste failure — bare catch block

Fixed

> 2. autoSubmit silently does nothing when no form is found

This one too noisy, if you want `autoSubmit` unconditionally specified in a wrapped component API, even if it's not in a form

> Test Coverage Gaps

Fixed

> Comment Improvements


Fixed
